description: Azure DevOps pull requests, work items and builds as first-class citizens: live link chips, issue tab, brokered agent tools, webhooks and a reconciler.
author: mzaferyahsi

jobs.description: Drains the webhook inbox and applies gated actions a person has approved.
Re-reads linked open pull requests and work items so lost webhooks heal.
Prunes the inbox, audit and effect tables and releases stuck inbox rows.
Runs the steps of an approved staging release bundle: build 140, pin the digest, deploy 138. Does nothing unless releaseBundle.enabled.

admin.description: Optional separate least-privilege identity used only by the platform administration tools. Secrets only as secret_ref; its secrets must differ from every other identity's.

platformAdmin.description: Governed Azure DevOps environment-check and Secure File permission tools. Off by default; an empty list allows nothing.

variableGroups.description: Library variable groups agents may ask to create or change (always confirmed by a person). Each secret variable is bound to a Paperclip secret here; agents never choose the secret.

deployApproval.description: Deploy approval plumbing only; default deny. Semantic validation enforces role separation and exact non-production environment membership.

tools.name: ado_release_bundle_create
tools.description: Propose ONE human-approved staging release: pipeline 140 builds the pinned commit of main, then pipeline 138 deploys the digest 140 published. A person decides on a card on the release issue; after approval the plugin worker runs both pipelines (never you), for 2 hours at most. Staging only, branch main only. Deploy still waits for the environment approval and the three attestations. You choose only the commit and a reason.

releaseIssue.description: Identifier of the release issue (assigned to you, in progress).

commit.description: Full commit id: the tip of main, or the merge commit of a completed pull request close to the tip.

tools.name: ado_release_bundle_get
tools.description: Status, time left, pinned tuple (commit, digest, build id) and the 138 run of a staging release bundle. Give bundleId or the release issue identifier.

tools.name: ado_release_bundle_revoke_apply
tools.description: Revoke a bundle with a reason. Narrowing only: no further step starts, and a deploy run still waiting at the environment approval is cancelled. A deploy run already approved and running is never cancelled.

tools.name: ado_release_verdict_post
tools.description: Attest one exact release commit, image digest and build. The release function comes from configuration; the deploy approver cannot attest. A later vote replaces an earlier vote on the same tuple.

tools.name: ado_environment_approval_get
tools.description: Read what the staging environment Approval check is waiting for, live, with every fact and a missing[] list of stable error codes. With approvalId it evaluates one approval; without it lists pending approvals on allowlisted environments only (max 20). Optional releaseIssue is needed to check attestations and blockers. Read only: nothing is decided. Requires platformAdmin.deployApproval.enabled.

project.description: Project name or id. Optional when exactly one project is configured.

tools.name: ado_environment_approval_post
tools.description: Approve or reject ONE pending staging environment Approval check by id. Approve only works when every condition holds live (environment, deploy pipeline, image digest, commit, build, release attestations, requester, release issue) and is applied by the plugin with the platform administration identity. Reject only works for a pending approval on an allowlisted environment of an allowlisted deploy pipeline. One decision per approval id; a repeat returns the first outcome. The audit row and the Azure DevOps comment name you and your run, never the administration identity.

project.description: Project name or id. Optional when exactly one project is configured.

tools.displayName: Create or change a Library variable group (gated)
tools.description: Two phases: a person must approve creating or changing one allowlisted Library variable group. Plain variables carry their value (shown on the approval card); secret variables are named only and take their value from the Paperclip secret bound in the plugin settings, so no secret value ever passes through you. Credential-looking names are refused as plain variables. Variables not listed are left alone; nothing is deleted. Requires platformAdmin.enabled.

tools.name: ado_pr_complete_apply
tools.description: Two phases. Phase 1 (no actionId) checks the pull request and asks for approval: a person on the issue, or the configured approver agents (ado_pr_approval_post) after the plugin has verified the verdicts. Phase 2 (actionId) completes it once approved. Branch policies always apply; policy bypass is never used.

tools.name: ado_pipeline_run_create
tools.description: Queue a pipeline run. Runs of protected pipelines or on protected branches need approval first (two phases, as for ado_pr_complete_apply): a person on the issue, or another approver agent (ado_pr_approval_post) when the company lets approvers decide; give a reason. Other runs start at once. Calling without actionId PROPOSES an attempt: if the same attempt is still pending you get that one back; if the previous matching one was already used, you get a new action that needs its own fresh approval (an approval is never reused). Calling with an actionId only CHECKS or REPLAYS that action: an applied one returns its result and queues nothing.

project.description: Project name or id. Optional when exactly one project is configured.

commit.description: Run exactly this commit (full hash). The approval is bound to it.

issueId.description: Optional: the issue to ask on. Default is the issue this run checked out. It must be assigned to you and in progress.

tools.name: ado_pr_policy_queue_apply
tools.description: Queue the Build policy of a pull request on its current head, like the Queue button in Azure DevOps. Use it when the policy is manual-queue-only or stale, instead of a generic pipeline run, which is not linked to the policy. Always approved first (two phases, as for ado_pipeline_run_create): a person on the issue, or an approver agent when the company lets approvers decide; give a reason. Calling without actionId PROPOSES an attempt (the approval is bound to the current head commit; if the same attempt is pending you get it back, and after it was used a new call needs a new approval). Calling with an actionId only CHECKS or REPLAYS that action. It changes no policy, vote or merge.

repository.description: Repository name or id inside the configured project.

issueId.description: Optional: the issue to ask on. Default is the issue this run checked out. It must be assigned to you and in progress.

tools.name: ado_pr_approval_get
tools.description: What an approver needs. For a pipeline run action (actionId): the project, pipeline, branch, reason and proposer. For a pull request: whether the current head commit has the required verdicts by function, a passing pipeline policy, no active review threads and a staging gate result where one is required, and why not if it is not ready. Facts come from the plugin ledger and live Azure DevOps state, never from comments.
